name: LATHE
expansion: Latent Activation Topology of Hidden Embeddings

intro.problem: The hidden layers of the classifiers used in long-lived-particle searches are rarely examined, and we do not yet know whether visualizing them is merely striking or genuinely useful, for instance as an n-dimensional heat map showing where in latent space background closure succeeds and fails.
intro.value: If it is useful, latent maps could diagnose failures, separate training objectives that score alike, guide architecture choices in TRUSS, and tie what a network learned back to physical inputs, as related work has begun to do for jet taggers [@khot2023][@komiske2020].
intro.approach: We treat this as exploration with an exit: map trained models in prediction space [@mao2024], compare their hidden layers [@kornblith2019][@davari2023], and trace training trajectories [@horoi2022], then run a pre-registered kill test asking whether map coordinates predict held-out closure better than hyperparameters alone.
intro.goals: The outcome is an honest verdict. If the kill test passes, an interactive explorer whose structures are stable across seeds becomes an analysis tool; if it fails, we record that the latent picture adds nothing a metrics table does not, and stop.

questions: Is a latent map useful at all, or only striking: does it predict anything a metrics table does not?
Could an n-dimensional heat map of closure over latent space show where and why the background estimate fails?
Which latent structures survive across seeds, and which are artifacts of the projection?

tagline: Exploratory: is the latent space worth looking at?

components.name: First attempts
components.subtitle: What gets built and run first
components.summary: Small, cheap probes chosen so that a negative answer arrives quickly. Each one reuses models that already exist or come out of the baseline re-run.

items.label: Probe set
items.detail: Carve out held-out events before cross-validation so every model is compared on data none of them trained on

items.label: Model space
items.detail: One point per trained model, distances from per-event predicted probabilities, embedded the way the training-manifold work does [@mao2024][@klabunde2025]

items.label: Event space
items.detail: Hidden-layer activations of a single model, compared across seeds and objectives with CKA and its known failure modes guarded [@kornblith2019][@davari2023]

items.label: Positive control
items.detail: A known change in training regime along the decorrelation sweep should show up as a kink in the model-space trajectory; if it does not, the map is not seeing real structure

items.label: Dead-unit census
items.detail: Count hidden units that never activate, which also feeds the connection sizing in TRUSS [@khot2023]

components.name: The heat-map idea
components.subtitle: Where this could become useful
components.summary: Color latent space by background closure, signal density, or per-event contribution to the closure error, so regions where the ABCD estimate breaks down become visible. This is the version of the idea that could earn its keep; it is not yet known whether such regions exist.

items.label: Intrinsic dimension
items.detail: Measure how many directions the representation actually uses before mapping it, with shuffled and untrained controls [@ansuini2019]

items.label: Stability
items.detail: Display only structures that persist across seeds and projection choices; mode connectivity tests whether two solutions are really distinct [@garipov2018]

components.name: Latent cross-attention
components.subtitle: Where dependence lives before the scores
components.summary: A background-only critic that lets one network's hidden layer attend to the other's, set against the same pairs with one side shuffled [@lopezpaz2017][@vaswani2017]. Per-event attention between the two latent spaces could show where dependence enters, which a global similarity score cannot.

items.label: Order-free
items.detail: Hidden units have no order, so attention runs without positions [@lee2019]; units of a plain network are single numbers and are grouped before use

items.label: Controls
items.detail: Read against two controls: a plain critic on the joined hidden layers [@lopezpaz2017], and the same model with attention fixed to uniform [@zaheer2017], LEXICON's control. A win must come from attention, not from having a learned critic or extra capacity

items.label: Grouping fixed first
items.detail: How hidden units are grouped into tokens is fixed before any result is seen, since a free grouping choice could manufacture structure

items.label: Against CKA
items.detail: Kept only if it separates closing from non-closing models where representation similarity does not [@kornblith2019]

items.label: Kill test
items.detail: Subject to the same pre-registered kill test as every other map coordinate

items.label: Attribution
items.detail: Attention maps are a cross-check, not an explanation [@jain2019]

items.label: Scope
items.detail: Latent maps only. The loss-landscape fingerprints come from too few trained models to train an attention model, so attention is not used there

components.name: Loss landscapes
components.subtitle: Fingerprints of trained models
components.summary: A second lens on the same models: measure the shape of the loss surface around each trained network, then ask whether that shape says anything about closure that the training settings do not already say. The public explorer holds the method and, later, the data.

items.label: Fingerprint
items.detail: Per trained model: both ends of the Hessian spectrum, its trace, loss slices along filter-normalised directions [@li2018], how much the classification and decorrelation pushes cancel in each layer, and interpolation barriers between seeds [@garipov2018]

items.label: Probe batch
items.detail: Each model is measured on its own held-out events. Every model is first checked against the outputs saved during training, so the probe measures the network that was trained

items.label: Curvature method
items.detail: Lanczos on Hessian-vector products. Plain power iteration was dropped after a side-by-side check showed it stopping early and missing negative curvature

items.label: Fair baseline
items.detail: Fingerprints must beat what is known without them: the training settings and how long each model trained. Early exploration showed curvature partly tracks training length, so that is now part of the baseline

items.label: Seed barriers
items.detail: Seeds split their data differently, so each pair is compared only on events both models held out. Barriers are read only after hidden units are matched between seeds

items.label: Exploration first
items.detail: Each look at the design data is declared in writing before it runs and recorded afterwards; the pre-registered kill test runs once, on models not yet trained

components.name: Kill test
components.subtitle: Pre-registered exit
components.summary: Before anything is built into a tool, test whether map- or landscape-derived quantities predict closure on held-out events better than the training settings and training length alone. If they do not, the project stops with that result written down.

links.title: Architecture search
links.text: If latent maps prove useful, their features become an input to TRUSS's architecture generation; the dead-unit census feeds its connection sizing either way.

links.title: Feature-level dependence probe
links.text: KERF runs the same two-sample test on the input features to check its joint background model; this is the latent-space version.

links.title: Attention trunk and controls
links.text: LEXICON already runs attention with a uniform-attention control; the latent cross-attention probe reuses that control rather than building its own.
